bounds.hard_cap_basis: CPU one-thread measurement 2026-11-01: batch 96 at N64 100 steps 0.145 s (about 14.5 s per 10000 steps); batch 18 at N256 50 steps 0.051 s (about 41 s per 40000 steps). A CPU-only estimate of the whole job is roughly 8-10 minutes, so the H100 is expected well under the cap. Not a measured runtime of the new algorithm.
bounds.memory: a few GB GPU, host RAM < 4 GiB
bounds.phase_order_and_partial: each phase writes and hashes its output before the next; if the cap is hit the run stops, later phases stay absent and the receipt says incomplete

controls_in_job: CPU tiny analytic heat-cosine control and wrong-sign mutation rejected
actual same-job CPU vs CUDA tiny solver discrepancy <1e-9 with float64 and TF32 disabled; CUDA required, never silently falling back
equations: u_t = u_xx + (a - u + u^2 v); v_t = d v_xx + (b - u^2 v); zero-flux on [0, L] (engineering/rd_diffusion/config.json); Strang exact DCT diffusion + RK4 reaction

fixed.ic: u0=a+b, v0=b/(a+b)^2 plus continuous cosine ic_modal(seed,K=20,L,N,eps*|u0|,eps*|v0|); same seed for target and every candidate, coefficients scaled to the domain length L

gates.A_absolute_amplitude: target u peak-to-peak at tau=200 >= 0.10 absolute model units. Evaluated for every target BEFORE any mode or spectral-ratio summary. A target below it is reported 'unpatterned: design success undefined' and kept.
gates.B_design_success: best raw RMS score <= 0.02 absolute AND gate A met. A method that does not reach it is reported as not reaching it.
gates.no_relaxation: thresholds are not changed after outcomes; failures are retained; no epsilon tuning; mode/spectral summaries are secondary and reported only after gate A

resolution.claim_limit: three configurations and one IC seed per target: a sparse consistency check, no convergence claim
resolution.comparison: candidate vs target both solved at the config with the target's ic_seed, compared on the common 64-point grid by analytic cosine projection (rd_numerics.audit.common_grid); plus candidate self-difference to its own base field

seed_generalisation.comparison: candidate vs true parameters under the same new seed, N64 dt 0.02; reported as RMS per seed, a measure of IC dependence, not of identifiability alone

independent_checks.selected: each method's selected candidate and the true parameters, per target

methods.accounting: every true solver evaluation counts, initialization included; no hidden evaluation; no target parameter or target field is visible to either method except through the score of an evaluated candidate

baseline.algorithm: torch.quasirandom.SobolEngine(dimension=2, scramble=True, seed=1000+target_index), first 64 points mapped affinely to the bounds
baseline.name: scrambled Sobol

optimizer.algorithm: 4 rounds x 16 evaluations. Round 1: first 16 points of SobolEngine(2, scramble=True, seed=2000+target_index) (counts as evaluations). Rounds 2-4: in unit-square coordinates take the 4 lowest-score evaluated points so far; mean = their mean; per-axis sd = max(population sd of the 4, 0.03); draw 16 points ~ Normal(mean, sd) with torch.Generator seeded 3000+10*target_index+round; clip to [0,1]. Failed candidates rank last.
optimizer.name: batched elite Gaussian search (diagonal)
optimizer.tuning: none after outcomes; constants above are final

methods.pairing: equal 64 true solver evaluations per target per method; six targets; n=6 is descriptive: no significance test and no claim about superiority beyond these six targets
methods.selection: selected candidate = the lowest-score evaluated point of that method (ties to the earlier evaluation); selection uses only the 64 scores

near_optimal_and_nonidentifiability: for each target, pool both methods' evaluations and list every point with score <= best + 0.005; report count and the d and L range of that set. A large range is nonidentifiability, not an error.
never_read: No outcome of the original RD/DDPM holdouts is read, used or reproduced. Original RD/DDPM source, protocols, holdouts and failed audits are preserved untouched.

negative_controls: wrong-parameter mutation: evaluate (d_true*1.5 clipped to 40, L_true) and (d_true, L swapped to the opposite bound): score must exceed 0.02 for at least one of them on each patterned target, else the score is not discriminating
wrong-IC mutation: true parameters with ic_seed+1: score must exceed the oracle by a measurable margin (>1e-6)
oracle_and_negatives.positive_oracle: evaluate the true parameters with the target's ic_seed; expected score 0 (<1e-12). Run as a separate validation control and never enters either method's candidate set or elite selection.
oracle_and_negatives.source_mutation: preflight refuses when any pinned source hash differs; a test flips one byte and requires refusal

scope: Synthetic numerical inverse-design exercise with the existing Schnakenberg solver. Not a fish, not measured, not DNA, no biological interpretation; all variables and time are model units. No DDPM acceleration claim.

score.definition: RMS over both channels and all 64 cells of the raw difference candidate-minus-target at tau=200 (model units, no normalisation)
score.failed_candidate: non-finite or |value|>1000 scores as failure; it is retained in the trace with score null and ranks last

config.use: K_modes=20, eps=0.05 for the continuous cosine IC

projection.use: common_grid analytic cosine projection reused for cross-resolution comparison

status: FROZEN before any target field, score or trace is computed

targets.generation: d_true, L_true ~ Uniform(bounds) from numpy default_rng(20261101) (d vector then L vector); ic_seed = 910000 + index. Parameters and seeds were drawn before any solver run and are listed here; the optimizer never receives them.
targets.target_field: solver output (u,v) at tau=200, N64, dt 0.02, at the true parameters and the target's ic_seed
